citation: Visaya, M. V. and Limbada, T. (2015). Gender Performance in Physics Practicals. Department of Pure and Applied Mathematics, University of Johannesburg. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Gender+Performance+in+Physics+Practicals
title: Three-semester physics practicals dataset of 74 University of Johannesburg students
description: A longitudinal dataset of 74 students (25 males and 49 females) taking analytical chemistry and food technology at the Doornfontein Campus, University of Johannesburg, gathered over three semesters. As the article states, "Only students with data for all four practicals in mechanics, thermodynamics, optics, and electricity for all three semesters are considered." All students were in the extended program course, split into groups with demonstrators changed every semester, and marks were recorded with a special Excel marking program.
requirements: Complete data for all four practicals across all three semesters for each student included
constraints: The authors note results may differ for students from a different course, and recommend analysis per semester because demonstrators differ each semester
target_learners: Extended-program physics practicals students in analytical chemistry and food technology
target_learning_goals: Tracking binary distinction performance in mechanics, thermodynamics, optics, electricity and overall mark across semesters
examples: The dataset supports the six binary questions Q0-Q5 covering gender and distinctions in OVM, mechanics, thermodynamics, optics and electricity
